findings.subject: sidebar
findings.summary: The default desktop Sidebar (side='left', collapsible offcanvas/icon) breaks under dir=rtl: the width-reserving gap lands on the right while the fixed panel stays on the physical left, over the content; the RTL story skips this path.
findings.evidence: sidebar.css:166-186 (left:0 / right:0, border-right/left by data-side), sidebar.css:36-40 + sidebar.tsx:296 (in-flow gap first in a flex row), sidebar.css:285-293 (inset margin-inline-start:0 assumes inline-start sidebar); grep 'rtl|dir(' in sidebar.css/tsx: no matches; sidebar.stories.tsx:210 RightToLeft uses collapsible='none'.
findings.fix: Make the side axis logical (inline-start/inline-end, keeping left/right as deprecated aliases) and position the container with inset-inline-start/end and border-inline-end/start; add a RightToLeft story with the default collapsible sidebar and a baseline.

findings.subject: text-ticker
findings.summary: autoPlay scrolls overflowing text forever with no way to pause or stop it, failing WCAG 2.2.2 (level A).
findings.evidence: text-ticker.tsx:23 autoPlay prop, :107 isAutoPlaying; text-ticker.css:101-107 animation infinite on [data-autoplay] and also on :hover/:focus-within; no pause control; marquee.tsx:86-97 shows the system's pattern for the same rule.
findings.fix: Pause the autoplaying marquee on hover and focus-within, and stop it after one or a few loops (or render a pause toggle like Marquee); add a test for the paused state.

findings.subject: text-ticker
findings.summary: With autoPlay under reduced motion the resting truncated line keeps the edge mask, so its first glyph is faded out.
findings.evidence: apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-textticker-themes-chromium-linux.png (the 'N' of 'Now playing' faded in all 8 cells); text-ticker.css:26-37 mask on [data-overflowing][data-autoplay]; reduced-motion block :118-139 does not clear it.
findings.fix: In the reduced-motion block set mask-image: none on the autoplay selector (and only apply the mask while the track animates).

findings.subject: text-ticker
findings.summary: The marquee loop always moves left, so in right-to-left text it scrolls the wrong way and leaves a blank edge.
findings.evidence: text-ticker.css:109-116 keyframes translateX(calc(-50% - gap/2)) with no direction variable; compare marquee.css:13-28 --marquee-dir; no RTL story in text-ticker.stories.tsx.
findings.fix: Add a --text-ticker-dir set to -1 under :dir(rtl) and multiply the translate by it, as Marquee does; add a RightToLeft story.

findings.subject: text-ticker
findings.summary: A caller ref replaces the internal measuring ref in marquee mode, so overflow is never detected.
findings.evidence: text-ticker.tsx:111 ref={containerRef} followed by {...props} at :117 (React 19 passes ref in props).
findings.fix: Destructure ref and merge it with containerRef (a callback that sets both).

findings.subject: text-ticker
findings.summary: No test covers the component's actual behaviour: overflow measurement, autoPlay, reduced motion or the resize path.
findings.evidence: text-ticker.test.tsx:7-51, five render/prop tests only.
findings.fix: Add tests that stub scrollWidth/clientWidth to drive data-overflowing, autoPlay gating, and ResizeObserver re-measurement.

findings.subject: text-ticker

findings.evidence: text-ticker.css:61-82 activation selectors; sidebar-nav-tree.tsx:37-41, 176-180, 277-279 wrap labels in TextTicker.

findings.subject: calendar
findings.summary: Localization and direction are only partly wired: the month dropdown ignores the locale prop, day labels append English words, and RTL depends on both an ancestor dir attribute and DayPicker's own dir prop.

findings.fix: Format with options.locale?.code, take the today/selected words from the caller's labels, read direction from context or computed style and pass it as dir, and add an RTL story.

findings.subject: carousel

findings.subject: carousel
findings.summary: Caller props override internal wiring: a ref on Carousel replaces the direction/cursor ref, and onClick or disabled on CarouselPrevious/Next replaces navigation.
findings.evidence: carousel.tsx:248-250 ref before {...props}; :361-364 and :384-387 onClick/disabled before {...props}.
findings.fix: Merge refs; compose onClick (call the caller's, then scroll unless defaultPrevented) as SidebarTrigger does (sidebar.tsx:316-319).

findings.subject: carousel

findings.fix: Handle keys in bubble phase and skip editable targets; map ArrowUp/Down for vertical; add a forced-colors rule (CanvasText rest, Highlight current).

findings.subject: carousel

findings.subject: marquee
findings.summary: Orientation is a boolean `vertical` instead of the contract's orientation axis, and the props type omits ref (the only component typed with ComponentPropsWithoutRef).
findings.evidence: marquee.tsx:12, :26; marquee-contract.ts:6 orientations horizontal|vertical with no default; grep ComponentPropsWithoutRef in ui-react components: 1 file.
findings.fix: Add orientation?: MarqueeOrientation (default 'horizontal' in the contract) and deprecate vertical; type props as ComponentProps<'div'>.

findings.subject: marquee
findings.summary: The pause toggle and running state are never captured, because visual tests run with reduced motion, which hides the toggle.
findings.evidence: apps/storybook/vitest.config.ts:109 reducedMotion 'reduce'; marquee.css:97-99; ui-react-marquee-pause-toggle-chromium-linux.png shows no toggle.
findings.fix: Give the PauseToggle story reducedMotion 'no-preference' with the animation paused (paused state is deterministic) so the toggle over content is baselined.

findings.subject: sidebar-nav-tree
findings.summary: Parts take no DOM props or ref, and SidebarNavCollapsibleItem has no uncontrolled mode (open and onOpenChange are required).
findings.evidence: sidebar-nav-tree.tsx:77-86, 128-152, 213-228, 285-293, 319-322 closed interfaces; :224-225 required open/onOpenChange.
findings.fix: Extend each props type with the wrapped element's props and spread them; add defaultOpen to SidebarNavCollapsibleItem.

findings.subject: sidebar-nav-tree
findings.summary: The section toggle's name is hardcoded English ('Expand X' / 'Collapse X') with no prop to localize it, and there is no RTL story.
findings.evidence: sidebar-nav-tree.tsx:254; sidebar-nav-tree.stories.tsx has no RightToLeft export.
findings.fix: Use a static, caller-provided toggle label (e.g. toggleLabel, defaulting to the section label) and rely on aria-expanded for state; add an RTL story.

findings.subject: sidebar-nav-tree
findings.summary: No phone story, and long labels rely on the hover/focus ticker, so truncated labels are unreadable on touch.
findings.evidence: grep viewport|phone|mobile in sidebar-nav-tree.stories.tsx = 0; text-ticker.css:61-82.
findings.fix: Add a DarkSidebarPhone-style story with long labels; resolve with r2-k07-frame-7.

findings.subject: table
findings.summary: Selected rows disappear in forced colors, and the horizontal scroll container is not keyboard-focusable or nameable.
findings.evidence: table.css:96-99, 248-253 (fill only, no forced-colors rule); table.tsx:41-47 container takes no props, no tabIndex.
findings.fix: Add a forced-colors rule for [data-state='selected']; accept containerProps (or tabIndex/aria-label when it overflows) on the scroll container.

findings.subject: table
findings.summary: The default md table ignores density: head height and cell padding are literal rem values.
findings.evidence: table.css:59 height 2.5rem, :60 padding-inline 0.625rem, :75 padding 0.625rem; only size='sm' reads --a63-row-padding-block-xs (:115).
findings.fix: Express md head height and cell padding with row/space tokens (--a63-row-padding-block-*, --a63-space-*) so compact density tightens them.

findings.subject: app-view
findings.summary: Default landmark names are music-app specific ('Library' for the panel, 'Player' for the docked bar), so other products ship wrong accessible names silently.
findings.evidence: app-view.tsx:94 bottomBarLabel='Player', :101 panelLabel='Library'.
findings.fix: Use neutral defaults (e.g. 'Sidebar', 'Toolbar') or require the label when the region is passed; mention it in the docs guidance.

findings.subject: text-ticker
findings.summary: marqueeSpeed is a loop duration in seconds, so a higher 'speed' is slower.
findings.evidence: text-ticker.tsx:41, :122 '--a63-text-ticker-duration': `${marqueeSpeed}s`.
findings.fix: Rename to marqueeDuration (keep marqueeSpeed as a deprecated alias) and document the unit.

findings.subject: calendar
findings.summary: The modern, aqua and retro calendars are visually identical; the declared archetypes do not show per theme.
findings.evidence: ui-react-calendar-themes-chromium-linux.png (only terminal differs).
findings.fix: Decide whether day cells and nav buttons should take the theme's control material (retro bevel, aqua gloss) like Button.

findings.subject: table
findings.summary: Numeric columns have no end alignment or tabular figures, so the Amount column in every baseline reads ragged.
findings.evidence: ui-react-table-themes-chromium-linux.png; table.css has no numeric treatment.
findings.fix: Add a documented numeric cell treatment (text-align:end, font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums), e.g. a data-numeric attribute.

findings.subject: sidebar-nav-tree
findings.summary: The link-row toggle changes its name with its state while also exposing aria-expanded, so state is announced twice.
findings.evidence: sidebar-nav-tree.tsx:253-258.
findings.fix: Keep a static name and let aria-expanded carry the state (folds into r2-k07-frame-23).

findings.subject: marquee
findings.summary: useReducedMotion decides the markup during render (toggle, role, tabIndex), so server and reduced-motion client markup differ on hydration.
findings.evidence: marquee.tsx:57-60, :86; apps/storybook/ssr/ssr.test.tsx only checks that renderToString succeeds.
findings.fix: Render the toggle and let CSS hide it under reduced motion (already done at marquee.css:97-99), and set the scroll-region attributes after mount.
